tldr: On Nov 1 a benchmark post reported a 17-point gap between agents running the same model across 21 MCP servers. On Nov 2 a Show HN project proposed cryptographic agent identity and Uber described an MCP Gateway governing 800+ servers.
whats_new: A Nov 4 write-up reports AI coding agents installing abandoned MCP servers with known security issues, adding supply-chain risk to the thread on agent-side MCP trust.
why_it_matters: MCP trust now has three open fronts: which client runs the server, which identity it presents, and which servers an agent is allowed to install at all.
take_for_builders: Allowlist MCP servers instead of letting coding agents pick them, audit installed servers for abandonment and known advisories, and pin the agent client alongside the model in MCP evals.

status.detail: Agent variance, identity and gateway governance are now joined by reports of agents installing vulnerable servers.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers
Arken proposes agent identity; Uber gates 800+ servers behind a gateway
Coding agents are installing abandoned MCP servers with known security issues

open_questions: Will other large engineering orgs publish MCP gateway designs for discovery, auth and auditing?
Will the 17-point agent-client gap be reproduced on other MCP server sets?
Will agent clients or registries start flagging abandoned or vulnerable MCP servers before install?
